### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.pick

### Question

I have three questions if possible:

1.Is it possible to add a selection cursor in `mini.pick`, similar to the Telescope image, where an icon appears on the selected option?
![imagen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/97c47e1d-431a-4ff9-9a70-5b359811488c)

2.Is there a way to separate the colors of `prompt_prefix` and `prompt_cursor`?
I would like the `prompt_prefix` (an icon) to be red and the `prompt_cursor` to keep its normal color (white text). Currently, everything appears red in the image.
![imagen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3bf677e7-a06d-40ca-8eeb-bb9342711f8b)
### One possible idea for how this could be configured: 
```lua
window.prompt_prefix = {">", "hl_groups"}
window.prompt_cursor = {"|", "hl_groups"}
```

I'm not sure if there's a correct way to achieve this or if `mini.pick` has an option for it.

3.How do you configure the search in `MiniPick.grep_live` so that patterns like `*.lua local foo` or `local foo *.lua` work, searching for `.lua` files and finding those words inside them?

comment_data.body:
> 1.Is it possible to add a selection cursor in `mini.pick`, similar to the Telescope image, where an icon appears on the selected option?

Yes, it should be possible by writing custom [`source.show`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/d0464ced00abfd9bbed196fa36ccf3b1691c6b2c/doc/mini-pick.txt#L360-L383). To get which item is current, use [`current_ind` in `get_picker_matches()` output](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/d0464ced00abfd9bbed196fa36ccf3b1691c6b2c/doc/mini-pick.txt#L1273).

Predicting next question here: no, it will not be built-in or behind another new configuration option.

> 2.Is there a way to separate the colors of `prompt_prefix` and `prompt_cursor`?

No, there is not. The whole prompt is highlighted with [`MiniPickPrompt`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/d0464ced00abfd9bbed196fa36ccf3b1691c6b2c/doc/mini-pick.txt#L131) highlight group.

I'll think about adding separate `MiniPickPromptPrefix` and `MiniPickPromptCursor`, but there is a fundamental issue. Prompt is implemented as title/footer which should be properly truncated if too wide. This is straightforward if the whole title/footer is a single string, but with separate highlighting it is not. It would require separate logic from all other modules which I'd like to avoid.

> 3.How do you configure the search in `MiniPick.grep_live` so that patterns like `*.lua local foo` or `local foo *.lua` work, searching for `.lua` files and finding those words inside them?

Through setting [`globs`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/d0464ced00abfd9bbed196fa36ccf3b1691c6b2c/doc/mini-pick.txt#L1136-L1140). Interactively it looks like this:
- `:Pick grep_live`.
- Press `<C-o>`, type `*.lua`, press `<CR>`. Notice that picker's title changed to include `(rg | *.lua)`.
- Proceed using `grep_live` as usual.

comment_data.body:
@krovuxdev, there are now [`MiniPickPromptCaret` and `MiniPickPromptPrefix` highlight groups](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/82c895e58d893bbbde8300277d6ceee813b15f63/doc/mini-pick.txt#L132-L133). After looking at code I realized that text truncation for title was suboptimal (as it always truncated from left even if there was caret there), so I had to adjust to always have caret visible. The solution then allowed for a reasonably straightforward way to add support for separate highlighting of caret and prefix (but dealing with the amount of [actual changes](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/commit/c8890c9f2b9e109766fc3679c8cdf82b7171865b) was not fun :( ).

And a heads up: `window.prompt_cursor` was renamed to `window.prompt_caret` for more consistency.

comment_data.body:
> 1. Is it possible to add a selection cursor in mini.pick, similar to the Telescope image, where an icon appears on the selected option?

It is now fully possible via using `get_picker_matches()` output: [shown_inds`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/bddfbfc4c1dbca6b852f512e554cf2e05c2960a8/doc/mini-pick.txt#L1279) and [`current_ind`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/bddfbfc4c1dbca6b852f512e554cf2e05c2960a8/doc/mini-pick.txt#L1275).

The most robust approach here is to actually not write global `config.source.show`, because it would override default `source.show` which are crucial for some pickers (prominent example is whether to use icons or not). I was test driving the following approach with wrapping already defined `source.show` inside callback for `MiniPickStart` `User` event and it seems to work fine:

```lua
-- Automatically wrap picker's `source.show` to do some extra work of showing
-- gutter sign. This is needed over defining global `config.source.show` to
-- account for picker-specific ways of showing items (like showing icons or
-- not, etc.).
local show_gutter_ns_id = vim.api.nvim_create_namespace('mini-pick-show-gutter')
local wrap_show_with_gutter = function()
  local picker_opts = MiniPick.get_picker_opts()
  local show_fun = picker_opts.source.show

  picker_opts.source.show = function(buf_id, items_to_show, query)
    show_fun(buf_id, items_to_show, query)

    -- Show fresh gutter as extmark with inline virtual text:
    -- "  " for non-current item, "> " for current
    vim.api.nvim_buf_clear_namespace(buf_id, show_gutter_ns_id, 0, -1)

    local matches = MiniPick.get_picker_matches()
    local shown_inds, cur_ind = matches.shown_inds, matches.current_ind
    if shown_inds == nil or cur_ind == nil then return end

    local prefix_extmark_opts = { virt_text = { { '  ', 'MiniPickNormal' } }, virt_text_pos = 'inline' }
    for i = 1, vim.api.nvim_buf_line_count(buf_id) do
      prefix_extmark_opts.virt_text[1][1] = (shown_inds[i] == cur_ind and cur_ind ~= nil) and '> ' or '  '
      vim.api.nvim_buf_set_extmark(buf_id, show_gutter_ns_id, i - 1, 0, prefix_extmark_opts)
    end
  end

  MiniPick.set_picker_opts(picker_opts)
end

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('User', { pattern = 'MiniPickStart', callback = wrap_show_with_gutter })
```

I was test driving the following approach with wrapping already defined source.show inside callback for MiniPickStart User event and it seems to work fine:
-- Automatically wrap picker's `source.show` to do some extra work of showing
-- gutter sign. This is needed over defining global `config.source.show` to
-- account for picker-specific ways of showing items (like showing icons or
-- not, etc.).
local show_gutter_ns_id = vim.api.nvim_create_namespace('mini-pick-show-gutter')
local wrap_show_with_gutter = function()
  local picker_opts = MiniPick.get_picker_opts()
  local show_fun = picker_opts.source.show

  picker_opts.source.show = function(buf_id, items_to_show, query)
    show_fun(buf_id, items_to_show, query)

    -- Show fresh gutter as extmark with inline virtual text:
    -- "  " for non-current item, "> " for current
    vim.api.nvim_buf_clear_namespace(buf_id, show_gutter_ns_id, 0, -1)

    local matches = MiniPick.get_picker_matches()
    local shown_inds, cur_ind = matches.shown_inds, matches.current_ind
    if shown_inds == nil or cur_ind == nil then return end

    local prefix_extmark_opts = { virt_text = { { '  ', 'MiniPickNormal' } }, virt_text_pos = 'inline' }
    for i = 1, vim.api.nvim_buf_line_count(buf_id) do
      prefix_extmark_opts.virt_text[1][1] = (shown_inds[i] == cur_ind and cur_ind ~= nil) and '> ' or '  '
      vim.api.nvim_buf_set_extmark(buf_id, show_gutter_ns_id, i - 1, 0, prefix_extmark_opts)
    end
  end

  MiniPick.set_picker_opts(picker_opts)
end

vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd('User', { pattern = 'MiniPickStart', callback = wrap_show_with_gutter })
